prime.problem: The wafer-ai list has 120 links, almost all primary sources, and it calls itself a reference, not a syllabus. Reading it top to bottom would sink weeks into ISA manuals and other vendors' chips before you learn a single mechanism.
prime.fits: The study plan behind the series map. The overview says which courses to take; this card says which outside reading goes with each course, how deeply, and in what order, including Kiely's book.
expect: cards first, then the named sections
the six gaps the list has
prime.goal: Decide for any resource whether to read it deeply, skim a named part or skip it, justify the call from your job, and plan the ~93 hours into weeks.

attend: What test separates a DEEP resource from a SKIM one, and why do the same kind of documents (papers) land in both?
Why does perf-3 carry the largest reading block, and what in the kernels course makes so many of its rows only SKIM?
Why does perf-7 have no DEEP rows at all, and where does its training half get its sources instead?
Which SKIP groups would you promote first if your job changed, and what makes them safe to skip now?
Why read Kiely's techniques chapter first and the mechanics chapters afterwards?

must: The list is a reference, not a syllabus → reading it in order spends time on 49 items no current task needs → triage every link by what the goal needs → 27 DEEP, 44 SKIM, 49 SKIP → about 93 hours instead of the whole list

Each card compresses a paper to one mechanism and one worked example → reading the card first gives the shape → the paper's named sections then read fast → but design-review details (edge cases, baselines) live only in the source → so cards alone aren't enough

Verdicts follow the job, not the resource → an NVIDIA-first inference goal pushes AMD/TPU/Trainium and production-kernel stacks to SKIP → a different job (a TPU shop, a kernel-writing role, platform work) promotes those groups → the plan is re-cut, not re-read

The list is inference-only → training breadth, unit economics, engine internals, gentle MoE, multi-LoRA and quality-vs-speed are missing → the series fills those gaps with extra cards and outside sources
elevated: Mechanism before production detail → CUTLASS 3.x, CuTe, TMA and tcgen05 are SKIP here only because the mechanism comes first → a production kernel role flips them straight to DEEP
reference: per-row time estimates and section numbers
the 9 GPU Mode lecture numbers (1, 2, 4, 8, 14, 12, 36, 7, 22) and the runners-up
Kiely's page ranges for each step
the hour arithmetic: 43.25 h DEEP, 42.80 h SKIM, 7.33 h book

compress.prompt: Course-level compress: from memory, write the plan as one rule plus one sentence per course. What do you read, in what order, and roughly how many hours does each course's table cost?
checklist: rule: the course's cards first, then only the sections its DEEP/SKIM rows name
DEEP ≈ read 80%+ and do the problems; SKIM ≈ the named 10–30%; SKIP ≈ open only when a task needs it
rough sizes: perf-1 ~3.5 h, perf-2 ~9 h, perf-3 ~24 h, perf-4 ~13.5 h, perf-5 ~13.5 h, perf-6 ~8.5 h, perf-7 ~3 h, plus GPU Mode ~11 h and Kiely ~7.3 h
total ≈ 93 h, about 12 weeks at 8 h/week, labs extra
the plan changes with the job: promote the matching SKIP group

retrieve.q: Explain why "cards first, then the named sections" beats both reading only the cards and reading only the papers.
answer: the card gives the mechanism and a worked example, so the paper reads fast
papers alone: no map, and you read sections you don't need
cards alone: missing the edge cases and baselines asked about in design reviews

retrieve.q: Walk through how you'd triage a new link someone adds to the list, from reading its title to assigning DEEP, SKIM or SKIP.
answer: ask which course's mechanism it teaches, if any
if it is the primary source for a core mechanism and short enough, DEEP
if only one section serves the goal, SKIM and name that section
if it is a reference manual, another vendor, a production niche or a spec, SKIP until a task needs it

retrieve.q: You join a company that runs on TPUs and does routing/platform work. What do you promote, what do you demote, and what does that cost in hours or risk?
answer: promote the Pallas and TPU docs from SKIP
demote the Hopper tuning guide to SKIP and perf-3's DEEP kernel rows toward SKIM
risk: less kernel depth, so you trust kernel numbers you can't check yourself

compare.q: The reading plan is organised by course; the stack card by layer. If you had only a week before starting on the engine team, which organisation would you use to pick your reading, and what would you miss?
answer: by layer: go straight to layer 4 (perf-5 DEEP rows: Orca, Sarathi-Serve, speculative decoding) and perf-4's KV rows
by course: you'd start at perf-1 and might not reach the engine in a week
what you'd miss: the roofline and step-time arithmetic that explains why the engine's choices work

compare.q: perf-1 needs about 3.5 hours of outside reading but perf-3 needs about 24. What about each course's content explains that gap, and does a smaller table mean the course matters less?
answer: perf-1 is arithmetic and a mental model; the cards cover most of it, with one DEEP blog and one DEEP doc
perf-3 is a practical skill: tuning kernels needs reproducing siboehm and the reduction ladder, plus many docs to skim
no: perf-1's material is used by every later course

predict.q: Before adding it up: at 6 hours a week instead of 8, how many weeks does the 93.4-hour plan take, and what share of the total is the perf-3 table alone?
predict.answer: About 15.6 weeks (93.4 ÷ 6). The perf-3 table is about 24 h (7.75 h DEEP + 16.08 h SKIM), roughly 26% of the whole plan, and that is before the GPU Mode lectures, most of which also pair with perf-3.

apply.task: Audit one course's table from the card. Add up perf-3's DEEP hours and SKIM hours row by row, check the total against the card's "~24 h", then write your own 3-week schedule at 8 h/week for perf-3's reading only, placing each DEEP row right after the card it pairs with.
apply.done: You get 7.75 h DEEP (0.5 + 0.75 + 1 + 3 + 2.5) and about 16.1 h SKIM across 15 rows, ≈ 23.8 h total, and your schedule fits in 24 h with every DEEP row after its card.
apply.hint: The SKIM rows include one 8 h book (PMPP) that alone is half the SKIM time; decide whether it goes first or last.

reflect: Which prediction did you get wrong: the number of weeks, or how much of the plan is kernels?
